x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
FOM admitted to Monaco stewards: the pitlane distance used to calculate Gasly's speeds was WRONG.

#F1 #Gasly #F1Fanrecap

facebook.long_form:
🏛️ The Monaco Grand Prix result is STILL in limbo — and we won't know the answer for at least two more weeks.

The FIA's International Court of Appeal heard arguments on Tuesday in Paris. McLaren and Red Bull both showed up to argue against the reinstatement of Pierre Gasly to third place after the chaos at Monaco. The panel of four judges listened. Then they went home. No verdict.

Here's a quick recap of how we got here:

At the Monaco Grand Prix, Gasly was given two 5-second time penalties for exceeding the pit lane speed limit. That initially dropped him from P3 to P7. But then it emerged that FOM — Formula One Management — had measured the pit lane distance incorrectly. The speeds used to calculate Gasly's infractions were based on wrong data. The stewards rescinded both penalties and restored Gasly to P3.

McLaren (who got Piastri back to P3 briefly) and Red Bull (supporting Hadjar at P4) appealed. Now the court has to decide whether the reinstatement was correct under the regulations, even accounting for the measurement error.

The verdict is expected in roughly two to three weeks — somewhere around September 8-15. Until then, Gasly officially keeps his Monaco podium. Championship points for Gasly, Hadjar, and Piastri remain officially recorded in current positions.

This one matters. Those points could swing the Constructor championship by the end of the season.

Who do you think SHOULD have the Monaco podium? 👇

facebook.long_form:
🔴 Ferrari is about to make a decision that could change the 2026 F1 championship.

This week — before the Monza entry deadline — Ferrari must confirm whether their ADUO-2 upgraded power unit will debut at the Italian Grand Prix on September 4-6.

The numbers are staggering for an engine upgrade: approximately 15 additional horsepower. Around 0.2 seconds per lap at Monza. A completely redesigned turbocharger and combustion chamber. Ferrari's own simulations reportedly call it the biggest power unit step of their entire 2026 season.

Why does this matter so much RIGHT NOW?

Because Kimi Antonelli — the championship leader by 59 points — is taking a penalty engine at Monza and will start from the back of the grid. In front of his home Tifosi. At the fastest track on the calendar.

Lewis Hamilton, sitting 53 points back from Antonelli, could have a clear shot at victory from a front-row start if the ADUO-2 delivers. A Monza win with Antonelli fighting from the back could cut the championship gap dramatically heading into the final stretch.

Ferrari energized. Hamilton energized. The ADUO-2 ready.

This week is when we find out if the 2026 title fight just got a whole lot closer. 🏆

stories.title: Antonelli Engine Penalty at Monza — Tifosi Watch Their Prodigy Start Last

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Kimi Antonelli will start the Italian Grand Prix from the back of the grid.

Full power unit change at Monza — his home race. In front of the Tifosi.

He leads by 59 points. 11 races to go.

This is F1's version of a boss level. 🎮

#F1 #Antonelli #F1Fanrecap

facebook.long_form:
🇮🇹 Kimi Antonelli will start the Italian Grand Prix from the back of the grid.

At his home race. In front of the Tifosi. At the fastest circuit on the Formula 1 calendar.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirmed the decision to take a full power unit change at Monza. The reasoning makes sense: Antonelli has accumulated too many component changes due to earlier reliability problems, and the penalty was inevitable. Monza — with its long straights and famous overtaking zones like Lesmo, Variante Chicane, and the run to Parabolica — gives a driver the best chance to recover from a back-of-grid start.

There's also a silver lining: a fresh engine means Antonelli gets a significant power advantage for the final 11 races of the season. A clean, fully-powered Mercedes engine could actually unlock stronger race pace for the championship run home.

Context on the title picture: Antonelli leads by 59 points over both George Russell and Lewis Hamilton (tied at 183, Russell holds tiebreaker), with Lando Norris at 159 in fourth. With 11 races remaining, the lead is genuinely solid — but losing 25+ points at Monza while rivals take big points could tighten things considerably.

The Tifosi are going to be rooting for him to come from 20th and challenge for the podium. It's going to be one of the most watched drives of the season.

Can Antonelli pull off an extraordinary recovery at his home race?

stories.title: Lando Norris — Is McLaren's No. 1 Now Antonelli's Biggest Title Threat?

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Lando Norris has won back-to-back F1 races.

He's 83 points behind Antonelli with 11 races left.

Antonelli starts LAST at Monza. Ferrari has a 15hp engine upgrade on the way.

Who's your money on now? 👀

#F1 #Norris #McLaren #F1Fanrecap

facebook.long_form:
🎯 The question a lot of F1 fans are starting to ask: is Lando Norris Kimi Antonelli's biggest rival for the 2026 World Championship?

After back-to-back race wins — including a commanding 11.5-second victory at the Dutch Grand Prix — Norris has moved to 159 points, sitting 83 behind Antonelli. With 11 races remaining and a maximum 275 points still available, Norris is mathematically alive.

Sky Sports raised this question directly after Zandvoort: has Norris become the biggest threat?

Here's the case FOR Norris:
- McLaren has the best race pace on a variety of track types
- The floor issue that plagued Oscar Piastri has NOT affected Norris — he has been the clean, consistent performer
- Antonelli's Monza penalty is a gift: Norris could gain 20-30 points in a single weekend
- Norris has shown in recent years he can string wins together when momentum is right

Here's the case AGAINST:
- 83 points is a lot, even with 11 races left
- George Russell (183 pts) and Lewis Hamilton (183 pts) are actually mathematically closer
- Ferrari's ADUO-2 could make Hamilton the more dangerous threat at high-speed circuits

But the storyline is there. Norris. 2 wins in a row. Antonelli about to start last.

👀 The next two Sundays could tell us a lot.
